_meta.indication: BELSOMRA (suvorexant) is indicated for the treatment of insomnia characterized by difficulties with sleep onset and/or sleep maintenance.
_meta.receipt_date: 08/29/2012 (FDA review cover page 'Received Date(s)'; note the approval letter separately states 'received August 30, 2012').

pivotal_trials.design: Parallel group, randomized, fixed-dose study comparing two fixed doses of suvorexant (low dose and high dose) or placebo for three months, randomized in a 2:3:3 ratio.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with insomnia, ages 18-87; 42% (N=429) were older than 65 years.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoints were change from baseline in subjective Total Sleep Time (sTST) and objective Wakefulness After Sleep Onset (WASO) (sleep maintenance), and change from baseline in subjective Time to Sleep Onset (sTSO) and objective Latency to Onset to Persistent Sleep (LPS) (sleep latency), at Months 1 and 3.
pivotal_trials.n: A total of 1022 patients were randomized (placebo 385, low dose 254, high dose 383).
pivotal_trials.result: Positive for sleep maintenance: at Month 3, high dose reduced WASO by -22.9 min (p<0.00001) and increased sTST by 19.7 min (p<0.00001) vs placebo; for sleep latency, high dose reduced LPS by -9.4 min (p=0.0004) and sTSO by -8.4 min (p=0.0002) at Month 3.

pivotal_trials.design: Parallel group, randomized, fixed-dose, placebo-controlled study of similar design to Study 28.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with insomnia, ages 18-86; 41% (N=410) were older than 65 years.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Same prespecified primary endpoints as Study 28: change from baseline in sTST and objective WASO (sleep maintenance) and in sTSO and objective LPS (sleep latency) at Months 1 and 3.
pivotal_trials.n: A total of 1019 patients were randomized (placebo 387, low dose 240, high dose 392).
pivotal_trials.result: Positive for sleep maintenance: at Month 3, high dose increased sTST by 25.1 min (p<0.00001) vs placebo and reduced WASO by -29.4 min (p<0.00001); for sleep latency, LPS failed at Month 3 (-3.6 min, p=0.27) but subjective sTSO was positive (-13.2 min, p=0.00003).

key_safety: The most common adverse reaction (>=5% and at least twice placebo) was somnolence (BELSOMRA 7%; placebo 3%). Daytime somnolence with impaired alertness and motor coordination (including impaired driving) is the principal risk and increases with dose. Other adverse reactions included headache (7% vs 6% placebo), dizziness (3% vs 2%), diarrhea, dry mouth, abnormal dreams, and cough.
target_moa: Suvorexant is a highly selective dual orexin receptor antagonist that blocks the binding of the wake-promoting neuropeptides orexin A and orexin B to receptors OX1R and OX2R, thereby inhibiting activation of wakefulness-promoting neurons and facilitating transition from wake to sleep.
modality: Small molecule (new chemical entity, orally administered tablet)

advisory_committee.vote: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee (May 22, 2013) found substantial evidence of efficacy for sleep onset (12 yes/4 no) and sleep maintenance (16 yes/0 no), and that the 15 mg and 20 mg doses were acceptably safe (15 yes/3 no); the committee was divided on the safety of the 30 mg and 40 mg doses (7 yes/8 no).

description.text: Added labeling describing suvorexant use in patients with Alzheimer's disease and insomnia

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the addition of language to sections 6 (Adverse Reactions), 8 (Use In Specific Populations), and 14 (Clinical Trials) to describe suvorexant use in patients with Alzheimer's disease and insomnia.

summary.text: NDA 204569 for suvorexant (a new chemical entity, dual orexin receptor antagonist) for insomnia was submitted under section 505(b) and approved August 13, 2014 via a standard review; it was reviewed by the Peripheral and Central Nervous System Advisory Committee, and the Controlled Substances Staff recommended Schedule IV scheduling under the Controlled Substances Act. The pediatric study requirement was waived.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated August 30, 2012, received August 30, 2012, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Belsomra (suvorexant, MK-4305) 5, 10, 15 and 20 mg oral tablets.
We also refer to our approval letter dated August 13, 2014, which contained the following error:
Based on the above, CSS recommended scheduling suvorexant as a Schedule IV substance under the Controlled Substances Act.
We are waiving the pediatric study requirement for this application because necessary studies are impossible or highly impracticable.
